levels.L1: Unit — pure Python logic in the API (e.g. onion/URL routing). No VM, no network, no app. Runs in milliseconds.
levels.L2: Integration — a real NixOS backend boots in a VM and its routing is checked over a transport. No app involved.
levels.L3: App usage — the SelfPrivacy app is driven like a user (open, navigate tabs, add a service, ...) against a running backend, and screen-recorded.

install_methods.label: auto test-VM
install_methods.desc: The self-contained NixOS test VM the L2 nixosTests spin up. Not a manual install.

install_methods.label: VM · same device
install_methods.desc: NixOS backend in VirtualBox on this Ubuntu host (build-and-run.sh).

install_methods.label: LAN · direct cable
install_methods.desc: Target netbooted over a direct ethernet cable (router out of path), installed via nixos-anywhere.
install_methods.topology:
direct cable, router OUT of path -- netboot install
  +--------+  ethernet   +--------+
  | laptop |------------>| target |   (192.168.100.x)
  +--------+             +--------+

install_methods.label: LAN · via router R (target wired)
install_methods.desc: Laptop on R's wifi, target wired to R. Needs R configured for netboot (preflight will tell you how).

install_methods.label: LAN · via router R (target wifi)
install_methods.desc: Laptop and target both on R's wifi. Needs R configured for netboot (preflight will tell you how).

install_methods.label: native · installer USB
install_methods.desc: Target installed from a bootable USB installer to its internal disk (manual boot).
install_methods.topology:
installer USB -> target internal disk (no laptop link)
  +-----+   +--------+
  | USB |-->| target |
  +-----+   +--------+

tests.name: onion URL routing
tests.desc: Unit-tests the API logic that rewrites service URLs for .onion path-routing (T1.1–T1.17).
tests.run:
# Pure unit test — no VM, no network, no target.
cd selfprivacy-api && nix run .#pytest-vm -- tests/test_onion_routing.py -q

tests.name: backend up + routing
tests.desc: Boots a NixOS backend in a VM and checks the API + nginx path routing are reachable over the transport (T2/T3).
tests.run:
# L2 integration: boots a NixOS backend in a throwaway test-VM and checks API + nginx path
# routing over the transport. No app, no real target.
cd Manager-Ubuntu-SelfPrivacy-Over-Tor/backend && nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.<L2-test>

installs.name: LAN · direct cable
installs.desc: Target netbooted over a direct ethernet cable (router out of path), wiped+installed via nixos-anywhere, then verified. Direct-cable installer IP is 192.168.100.50; note the post-install public verify needs the box on the router (re-cable) or TRANSPORT=onion.
installs.run:
# FULL end-to-end: wipe target disks -> install SelfPrivacy (NixOS) -> verify.
# dash runs a PREFLIGHT for this --on first and refuses with instructions if the setup isn't ready.
# Override IP:  ./dash run <id> --ip <addr>   (or IP=<addr>); if the box isn't at that IP the e2e auto-discovers it on the LAN by MAC.
IP=<TARGET_LAN_IP> MAC=<TARGET_NIC_MAC> KEY=~/.ssh/<DEPLOY_KEY> DOMAIN=<YOUR_DOMAIN> TRANSPORT=https \
  FLAKE=<PATH_TO_DEPLOY_FLAKE> EXTRA=$FLAKE/state/extra dev-dashboard/tools/e2e_install_native_ethernet.sh
